correction.text: Pomerelia, Gdańsk Pomerania: the Duchy of Gdańsk and the Duchy of Świecie and Lubiszewo

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row; eu-15-d asked for a Pomerelia dossier). 'In 1227, the duchy gained independence from Poland', divided into the Duchy of Gdańsk and the Duchy of Świecie and Lubiszewo, unified under Mestwin II in 1270. The page gives no area; the gazetteer's Pomerelia region is the stand-in. The Sławno and Słupsk lands, partly lost to Barnim III after 1266 and held by Mestwin as a Brandenburg fief from 1273, are not in the shape.

region.text: Pomerelia, Gdańsk Pomerania: the Duchy of Gdańsk and the Duchy of Świecie and Lubiszewo

ledger.note: 1227: Pomerelia becomes independent. 'In 1227, the duchy gained independence from Poland' and was divided into the Duchy of Gdańsk and the Duchy of Świecie and Lubiszewo; Świętopełk II 'gained full independence in 1227' (reign 1213/20-1227).

region.text: Pomerelia, Gdańsk Pomerania: the Duchy of Gdańsk and the Duchy of Świecie and Lubiszewo

ledger.note: 1270: Gdańsk and Świecie are united. Infobox '1270 (unification of Gdańsk and Świecie)'; 'With the margraves' aid, Mestwin II succeeded in expelling Wartislaw from Gdansk in 1270/71'.
1270/71: Brandenburg troops hold Gdańsk. Mestwin II expelled Wartislaw 'with the margraves' aid' in 1270/71; in 1273 'the margraves, who refused to leave Gdańsk' were in 'open conflict' with him.
1273: 'Brandenburg returned Gdańsk to Mestwin while he paid feudal homage to the margraves' for Sławno and Słupsk.

region.text: Pomerelia, Gdańsk Pomerania: the Duchy of Gdańsk and the Duchy of Świecie and Lubiszewo

ledger.note: Summer 1308: 'a rebellion was incited by the local Swienca family' and Brandenburg intervened, occupying the duchy's west (Pomerelia page: 'the city of Gdańsk was occupied by the Margraviate of Brandenburg' in 1308). The Teutonic text gives the season only.

region.text: Pomerelia, Gdańsk Pomerania: the Duchy of Gdańsk and the Duchy of Świecie and Lubiszewo

ledger.note: 1308: the Teutonic Order, invited by Władysław's governor Bogusza, enters the duchy; on 13 November 1308 'the order's forces ... forced their way into the town' of Gdańsk, which was captured and largely destroyed. The Order 'evicted the Brandenburgers but took the area for themselves'.
13 November 1308: Gdańsk falls to the Teutonic Order.

region.text: Pomerelia, Gdańsk Pomerania: the Duchy of Gdańsk and the Duchy of Świecie and Lubiszewo

ledger.note: September 1309: 'Margrave Waldemar of Brandenburg-Stendal sold his claim to the territory' to the Order for 10,000 marks (Treaty of Soldin).

region.text: Pomerelia, Gdańsk Pomerania: the Duchy of Gdańsk and the Duchy of Świecie and Lubiszewo

ledger.note: September 1309: the Treaty of Soldin ends the contest; the Order holds the whole duchy.

region.text: Pomerelia, Gdańsk Pomerania: the Duchy of Gdańsk and the Duchy of Świecie and Lubiszewo

ledger.note: 1309: 'The Order took the whole duchy after the Treaty of Soldin'; the Pomerelia page: the Teutonic Knights took the area, 'annexing and incorporating it into the Teutonic Order state in 1309'. Świecie and Tczew were conquered after Poland refused compensation for Gdańsk.

region.text: Pomerelia, Gdańsk Pomerania: the Duchy of Gdańsk and the Duchy of Świecie and Lubiszewo

ledger.note: 1309: the Duchy of Pomerelia is annexed into the State of the Teutonic Order; the infobox lists it as a fiefdom of Poland (1294-1308).

wars.name: Świętopełk II's wars with the Teutonic Order
wars.outcome: The Old Prussian revolt of 1242 came 'in the context of these alliances'; peace came with the Treaty of Christburg in 1249 and the Vistula-dues settlement of 1253.

wars.name: Mestwin II's war with Wartislaw and Brandenburg
wars.outcome: Mestwin expelled Wartislaw from Gdańsk with the margraves' aid in 1270/71; the margraves stayed until the 1273 treaty returned Gdańsk against homage for Sławno and Słupsk.

wars.name: Teutonic takeover of Gdańsk

zones.text: Pomerelia, Gdańsk Pomerania: the Duchy of Gdańsk and the Duchy of Świecie and Lubiszewo

wars.outcome: Brandenburg occupied the west in summer 1308; the Order took Gdańsk on 13 November 1308, then the whole duchy after the Treaty of Soldin in September 1309.

certainty.note: The pages give cities (Gdańsk, Świecie, Tczew, Sławno, Słupsk) and rivers, not boundaries; the western frontier with the Pomeranian dukes moved by dukes' agreements.

notes:
Duchy of Pomerelia is a state Cliopatria lacks (eu-15-d asked for it as [1282, 1294]); the page's wider life 1227-1309 is used, with the earlier Polish fiefdoms (1119-1210) and the Danish one (1210-1211) left out. Not drawn as such by the Polish rows after 1227.

Not settled: (1) The vassal relations belong to the overlords' ledgers: homage to Brandenburg (Treaty of Arnswalde/Choszczno, 1269, and 1273 for Sławno and Słupsk), Przemysł II's suzerainty by the Treaty of Kępno (15 February 1282, duchy-of-greater-poland), the Polish fief 1294-1308; Władysław lost Greater Poland and Pomerelia in 1300 after a nobility revolt and 'recaptured' Pomerelia in 1306 (page), and sold his Kraków rights to Wenceslaus II in 1297. Those events need vassal_start/vassal_end naming duchy-of-pomerelia in duchy-of-greater-poland, kingdom-of-poland and kingdom-of-bohemia. (2) Brandenburg's 1308 occupation covers 'the duchy's west' per the Teutonic page; the region is the whole duchy as a bridge (confidence 2). (3) The division between the Duchy of Gdańsk and the Duchy of Świecie 1227-1270 is not drawn. (4) Area not on either page. (5) The Mestwin II reign years are not on the page, so no rulers list. Counterpart 'Duchy of Świecie (Wartislaw)' is a name, not a dossier.
